tip: कौन (kaun) = who. कौन is for people: कौन है? (who is?). क्या is for things.
कौन सा (kaun sa) = which (m). For f: कौन सी. For pl: कौन से. Picks one item from many.
कितने बजे हैं? (kitne baje hain?) = literally "how many struck have?" = what time is it? Memorize as a phrase.
कितने का (kitne ka) for masculine items, कितने की for feminine. Used in shop questions: यह कितने का है? = how much is this?
X से (X se) = from X. मैं X से हूँ = I am from X. Swap लंदन for any city.
कितने (kitne) = how many. कितने लोग? (how many people). कितनी for feminine items.
किसका (kiska) = whose (for m thing). किसकी for f, किसके for plural. यह किसकी किताब है? = whose book is this?
फिल्म (film) is feminine in Hindi, so the adjective ends in -ी: अच्छी (achchi, good-f). For m: अच्छा.

english: The book is on the table.
tip: पर (par) = on. Comes after the noun: मेज़ पर (mez par = on the table). Hindi puts position words after.

english: The chair is in the room.
tip: कमरा (kamra = room) shifts to कमरे (kamre) before में (mein). Masculine -आ nouns usually change to -ए before position words.
ख़राब (kharab = broken / bad). Used for objects (broken) and food (gone bad): दूध ख़राब है = the milk has gone bad.
There's no verb 'to know' here – knowledge sits on you: मुझे नहीं पता (mujhe nahin pata) is literally 'to me it is not known'. मुझे (mujhe = to me) does the work.
